Did you not see The Killer? It was a major production and was very popular when it came out on Netflix akin to that of a theatre release in terms on online discussion. Maybe this post would have made sense before 2023 but you can’t really says someone is in “director jail” when he just released a 100m movie with a major cast and distribution last year
He seems to be able to do what he wants at Netflix and the results are excellent. The Killer was one of last year’s best. Not sure how you could reasonably consider that director jail.

I think many directors feel pretty disillusioned with Hollywood recently and have had a much easier time finding funding with streaming services. I don't know enough about Fincher to know if he's burned any bridges, I thought he was still generally people's good graces. I'm not sure he's in director jail, though, or at least no more than every other major arthouse director

No, he is not in director jail.  Netflix is part of Hollywood and considering the budgets of their projects, they are a major studio. He does not want to work with the traditional majors, not vice versa.  More films fail to complete production than do, and all directors have a long list of unrealized projects.
Why does it feel like The Killer was like 5 years ago?

He directed Mank which was up for multiple Oscars. It's not "hollywood" as it was netflix and not a movie studio, but I think it's something.

  
he also had a different gig between 2016-2019. Per his wikipedia:

\>Between 2016 and 2019, Fincher directed, produced and served as showrunner for another series, [*Mindhunter*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindhunter_(TV_series))
Not to mention it's easily one of the most unapologetically Fincher films Fincher has done to the point where he is pretty much making fun of himself.
They say time is the fire in which we all burn
It does? It's still very fresh in my mind and I went to the premiere almost a full year ago.
I wouldn't call Mank excellent, but your point is taken.

Most Americans aged at least four years between June 27 and July 21 of this year.

If he is in jail, it’s purely voluntary and he can get out anytime he wants.

He’s worked a lot with Netflix over the last decade where they even signed him to a four year deal in 2020 that just got renewed for another three years. My guess is they give him a lot more creative freedom than other studios. I can’t imagine a lot of people not wanting to work with him considering all the accolades that his films garner.

Ultimately, I think it just comes down to he’s doing his own thing similarly to James Cameron.

> It doesn't seem like he can get a non streaming project off the ground or completed. 

What films are you referring to, which projects can't he get off the ground, and which has he started and cannot get completed?

> we all know David Fincher is one of the best directors of our time

He's a great craftsman. He's not an auteur. When we talk about best directors we often are talking about auteurs. Even when Scorsese or Scott misfires, it's an interesting misfire worthy of discussion. Gangs of New York, Napoleon. Fincher movies tend to blend into the background, and when they're not great, they're also not that interesting. 

From previous discussions:

* Fincher hasn't really blown people away since Zodiac

* someone [like him] who makes movies like IKEA makes furniture (solid, versatile, but without any real personality) gives an audience less to debate and discuss

* all of his movies uncomfortably over-identify with quippy sociopaths, especially when he forces it on a story like Mank, where it really didn't belong

Fincher seems *perfect* for streaming. He helped to invent streaming series. He's not someone who needs to make features, or who needs to make series, he can do both.  Hollywood is still interested in box office, and Fincher is not able to operate there on the level of Nolan or Villeneuve. He also doesn't seem interesting in cranking out content, like M. Night does.

As for burned bridges, I doubt that. If someone makes money and wins awards, they can leave a mountain of ashes in their wake and nobody cares. 

That said, while The Killer and Mank weren't up to par with previous works (for me) they certainly had big Hollywood budgets. You don't get that sort of money in jail.

But not what we want... SEASON 3 OF MINDHUNTER WHEN!? 

lol

Unlike Rian Johnson, Fincher isn't a hypocrite.

He goes to Netflix because he wants the most control and he is willing to cede theatrical distribution to get it.

"Mank" and "The Killer" were long-time projects that he couldn't enlist the interests or studios to finance.

>akin to that of a theatre release in terms on online discussion.

Not to mention, it did, in fact, get limited theatrical releases 2 weeks prior to streaming. In various international territories. You are right, though. The majority of reactions came in right after streaming.
Mank and the killer are subpar at best.

Fincher is apparently extremely picky and detail oriented, he likes to tweak tiny details nobody would notice with CGI. I think he was never a super mainstream director and Netflix has given him enough creative control to keep him there. I guess you could call it a gilded cage but he's getting to make his movies the way he wants to make them. 


You could ask the same question about jean-pierre jeunet too,I read that he once said Netflix would be a last resort for him and his last movie came out on Netflix with very little buzz.
Yeah, the film is pretty funny and I'm sure each rewatch that's more blatant
I mean agree to disagree I guess, The Killer was in my top 5 for last year.
Yes you are right but it did less than 500k in theatres so really wasn’t even a full release. I wish it had gone full 3000+ theatres because I think it would have done quite well
Unironically though. He's in my personal director jail for ditching that series.
Yeah Mank was a passionate failure sadly. He's too obsessed with digital lol. whole uncanny valley film
What did Rian Johnson do?

Leaked a story (two years after the fact) about Daniel Craig throwing a fit at the premiere of "Glass Onion" over the film's theatrical distribution ... as if that will make everyone forget that Johnson and co took $400 million from Netflix.

I can guarantee that Fincher and many of their colleagues rolled their eyes when they read that story.

You either accept the Netflix money or you don't.

Don't whine two years later that Netflix chose a Netflix model to distribute a Netflix film.
I see, I wasn't aware, thanks for sharing.
The Killer was like the most 7/10 movie I've ever seen. It was...good? Kinda? I enjoyed it... I think? But I have no idea why and I'll never watch it again.
I agree, if he followed up Aliens 3 with The Killer instead of Se7en, I don't think he'd have escaped his rocky start.
I don't buy for a minute that Fincher intended it as self-parody.
All that effort to sound old and then you shoot in a widescreen ratio, not in Academy, ignoring any issues with digital photography and the actual film.
Mindhunter was also incredible. Sad that we probably will never get more of it.

I think the whole industry is in jail and looking for ways out. Many have migrated to Netflix, not because it’s great - but because it’s one of the last refuges directors have to produce their own work carte Blanche. Say what you want about Netflix (I’ve thrown a lot of shade:) but they do pretty much let directors like Fincher, Scorsese, Cuaron alone to do their thing. 

Fincher actually fits pretty well there since he’s always claimed to never care about neither format nor distribution. He was one of the first to embrace digital cameras and thus it’s natural for him to embrace digital / streaming distribution. Whatever the scale, as long as he can do his thing without bother. 

Do I miss when movies like Se7en or the Social Network were actual theatrical event movies? Yes. Won’t happen right now. Maybe not ever again. Instinctively I think the directors in the industry know this. Which is why Cuaron has gone on to series. And Scorsese is on Netflix and Apple. 

Only a few auteur directors can command (and basically require in their contracts) theatrical releases for their films - Wes Anderson, Spielberg, PTA, Nolan and Tarantino. They seem now the exception rather than the rule
He’s a wannabe Kubrick
7/10 is a very strong rating, so not sure what you’re saying with that.
I guess rating scales are arbitrary. For me 7 is "good" and it borders on that. It's an Ok to Good movie. It's certainly not very strong in my eyes anyway.

It’s very strong. 70% is more than adequate. It equates to good-low great on the 5 point scale, around 3 -3.5 stars out of 5. 

An average, competent film that is in no way offensive nor commendable is a 50%.

Im not going to debate about one made up scale vs another made up scale. 70% is a C-

The Killer was ok. 

I wish you well.

American school grades are so funny to me. They’re pretty much meaningless these days because a kid can literally never go to class and get a 70%, so a C- is the new F.  But they aren’t really relevant to this discussion.

It isn’t arbitrary. It’s a hundred point scale. An average film would fall in the middle, at 50%. Or 2.5 out of 5, or 5 out of 10. 5 is the pure average.
